chapters.title: The Problem of Extreme Complexity
chapters.sourcePressure: The opening diagnosis uses the Austrian drowning rescue, superspecialists, and the limits of lone mastery to show why avoidable failure persists inside expert work.
chapters.coreMove: Spot when a system has become too complex to trust to memory and individual command alone.
chapters.commonMisread: Turn it into a vague sermon that people should be more careful or try harder.

chapters.title: The Checklist
chapters.sourcePressure: The B-17 story and Pronovost's central-line work show that one missed basic can beat expertise, and a short checklist can prevent routine omissions.
chapters.coreMove: Separate vital minimum checks from expert knowledge and make those checks visible at the moment they are skipped.
chapters.commonMisread: Make checklists sound like general to-do lists or productivity hacks.

chapters.title: The End of the Master Builder
chapters.sourcePressure: Simple, complicated, and complex problems plus Russia Wharf show that modern projects are too distributed for one master builder to command.
chapters.coreMove: Replace the master-controller reflex with distributed coordination and explicit handoffs.
chapters.commonMisread: Praise collaboration in generic terms without naming the control problem.

chapters.title: The Idea
chapters.sourcePressure: The Katrina and Wal-Mart contrast shows how local action needs disciplined communication rather than trapped central permission.
chapters.coreMove: Let people act near the facts while using short communication checks to keep the system aligned.
chapters.commonMisread: Turn decentralization into a loose permission slip with no shared signal.

chapters.title: The First Try
chapters.sourcePressure: The early WHO surgical-checklist pilot surfaces resistance and refinement, showing that an idea becomes usable only after friction teaches the design.
chapters.coreMove: Treat first-use resistance as implementation data and revise the checklist until the vital pause survives real workflow.
chapters.commonMisread: Frame resistance as mere stubbornness or say the first draft just needs buy-in.

chapters.title: The Checklist Factory
chapters.sourcePressure: Dan Boorman, Boeing manuals, and simulator learning show that checklist quality is a design discipline built around brevity, timing, and live usefulness.
chapters.coreMove: Design the list for the pressure point, cutting everything that does not earn attention in live execution.
chapters.commonMisread: Assume a better checklist is a more complete checklist.

chapters.title: The Test
chapters.sourcePressure: The WHO 19-item checklist, Do-Confirm versus Read-Do, and the eight-hospital test show whether the tool survives real variation.
chapters.coreMove: Raise confidence from local promise to field evidence by testing the checklist across different conditions.
chapters.commonMisread: Celebrate a single successful pilot as proof.

chapters.title: The Hero in the Age of Checklists
chapters.sourcePressure: Once evidence exists, resistance shifts to ego, professional identity, lone-hero mythology, and the acceptance of disciplined teamwork.
chapters.coreMove: Redefine professional excellence so shared verification counts as strength rather than insult.
chapters.commonMisread: Scold experts for arrogance without understanding the identity threat.

chapters.title: The Save
chapters.sourcePressure: The closing chapter uses investing and Mohnish Pabrai to show checklist logic outside surgery while preserving domain fit and judgment.
chapters.coreMove: Transfer checklist discipline to another field by rebuilding it around that field's recurring failure points.
chapters.commonMisread: Claim every domain should copy surgical routines unchanged.
